You are part of an optimization system that improves a given text (i.e. the variable). You are the gradient (feedback) engine. Your only responsibility is to give intelligent and creative feedback and constructive criticism to variables, given an objective specified in <OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION> </OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION> tags. The variables may be solutions to problems, prompts to language models, code, or any other text-based variable. Pay attention to the role description of the variable, and the context in which it is used. You should assume that the variable will be used in a similar context in the future. Only provide strategies, explanations, and methods to change in the variable. DO NOT propose a new version of the variable, that will be the job of the optimizer. Your only job is to send feedback and criticism (compute 'gradients'). For instance, feedback can be in the form of 'Since language models have the X failure mode...', 'Adding X can fix this error because...', 'Removing X can improve the objective function because...', 'Changing X to Y would fix the mistake ...', that gets at the downstream objective.

# - <LM_INPUT>: The input to the language model.
# - <LM_OUTPUT>: The output of the language model.
# - <OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION>: The objective of the optimization task.
# - <VARIABLE>: Specifies the span of the variable.
# - <ROLE>: The role description of the variable.
payload.instruction: Turn the image into a drawing made from chalk
payload.rubric: Judge requested image editing: yes means all requested changes are complete, no means no requested change has progressed, partial means some progress without complete fulfillment. Unrelated edits are not requested progress. Insufficient evidence stays unresolved.

node.question: Compared with the source, has the image been transformed into a coherent chalk drawing, or does it show meaningful chalk-rendering progress without completing that transformation?
node.criteria: Pass only when the main subjects and surrounding scene are rendered as a coherent chalk-made drawing: drawing-like forms and chalk marks replace substantial source-like photographic anatomy, patterns, and scene detail in both subjects and background. Fail when there is no meaningful requested chalk-drawing change. If chalk rendering meaningfully changes the image but substantial photographic structure remains in either the subjects or background, fail this completion condition; that evidence represents partial progress, not no progress. Texture, scene-wide coverage, or recognizable chalk effects alone do not establish completion. Unknown if the source or edited image is unavailable or evidence is insufficient to judge.
node.binding: Compare the source and edited images. Assess whether drawing-like forms and chalk rendering replace substantial source-like photographic structure separately in the subjects and background. Keep the completion threshold strict: residual substantial photographic structure in either means the requested transformation is incomplete. Also distinguish meaningful chalk-rendering changes from no requested change: chalk-like grain, softened contours, or smudged shading that visibly alters the image can be progress even when it does not satisfy completion. Do not infer completion from texture or coverage alone, and do not count unrelated edits as progress. Judge the requested chalk-medium transformation, not a particular style.

node_traces.evidence: The edit adds a visible grainy, smudged chalk-like treatment across the scene, so there is meaningful chalk-rendering progress. However, both giraffes retain substantial photographic anatomy and recognizable coat patterns, and the background retains photographic scene structure despite its softened, streaked appearance. The strict completion condition is therefore not met.
